claim_checks.source: Theorem 1.2 p. 3, whole-plane transfer p. 5; boundary-trace context p. 2 and construction p. 7
claim_checks.independent_reason: The theorem admits all W^(1,infinity) intersect L1 half-plane data of sup norm one and imposes no zero boundary trace. The Gaussian exp(-x^2-y^2) has L1 norm pi/2 and gradient norm sqrt(2/e), but its odd extension has normal derivative -2|y| exp(-x^2-y^2)+2exp(-x^2)delta_(y=0). It is not W^(1,infinity). The proof's all-pairs Lipschitz comparison, then rotations, therefore cannot substitute the half-plane gradient bound into that whole-plane estimate.
claim_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: Bounded-vorticity reflection, Biot-Savart and the coarser separation estimate still work; the lower-growth construction is not refuted. A direct half-plane strain proof could possibly repair the sharp upper estimate but was not supplied or certified. Because the sharp upper rate is used for exact maximality, the demonstrated core proof gap supports Major.
claim_checks.correction_scope: Retain the exact gap and required repair. Do not assert that Theorem 1.2 is false or that imposing zero trace covers the original full scope.
